title: A Quiz That Doesn’t Like You
dek: Ten questions. Every answer is in this issue. Every wrong answer is too, which is the mean part.
summary: A ten-question multiple-choice quiz on the issue’s stories, from Napoleon’s coup and Carthage to the Emu War and Ross Perot, with answers.

blocks.text: Side Eye Assessment Service · Form L-1 · Section: Losing · Time: Until you give up
Use a No. 2 pencil. Fill each bubble completely. Every answer is in this issue. So is every wrong answer.
1. Emmanuel Sieyès spent 1799 “looking for a sword.” Which two generals did he try before Napoleon?
2. In late September 1799, a 100-franc French government bond sold for about 7 francs. What was it worth within a week of the coup?
3. The Roman Senate had exactly one Carthaginian book translated into Latin. What was it about?
4. In Madison’s notes from March 28, 1783, one ratio for counting enslaved people was voted down just before he proposed “5 to 3.” Which one?
5. In 1862 Lincoln argued the border states’ enslaved people could be bought for less than how many days’ cost of the war?
Form L-1 · Continued · Do not fold, spindle or mutilate

6. In 1844 John C. Calhoun cited 1840 census figures on insanity among free Black Northerners. What had a Massachusetts doctor already shown about the 133 “coloured lunatics and idiots” listed in Worcester?

items: B. A clerk added the column by mistake
C. They had escaped from Virginia
D. They were the white patients in the state hospital

blocks.text: 7. The veterans’ 1920 rulebook asked Southern librarians to write three words on the title page of every book that failed it. Which three?
8. On November 8, 1932, newspaper paragraphs pulled the machine guns out of the Emu War. What sent them back?

items: C. Protests from the wheat areas and Western Australia’s premier

blocks.text: 9. Major Meredith reported 986 confirmed emu kills. From how many rounds?
10. According to the Iran-Contra independent counsel, how much did Ross Perot “make available” for Oliver North’s hostage operation?
Name the free man honored as a “faithful” slave on the 1931 stone at Harpers Ferry.
Answer sheet: 1–10, bubbles A B C D. Score ____/10. Pencils down.
Answers are printed upside down and backward on the inside back cover, because we are not above it.

blocks.title: A Quiz That Doesn’t Like You · Answers (printed upside down on p. 111)

blocks.text: 10 right: You’re a Director now. Please don’t overthrow anyone. 7-9: Lucien Bonaparte would lend you his sword. 4-6: Your bonds are holding at 11.38. 1-3: You took the Sacko. We’re proud of you. 0: The emus would like a word.

sources: Every answer is in this issue: questions 1–2 draw on the Napoleon feature; 3 on Two Libraries and The Loser’s Library; 4–7 and the tiebreaker on the Civil War feature; 8–9 on the Emu War feature (Meredith’s figures are his own, unpublished); 10 on the Perot feature.
